Definition: Whether an official government web portal or mobile application exists where taxpayers can file tax returns and pay taxes online with direct e-payment capability linked to instant payment system.
Comments: 0: Searched for Egyptian Tax Authority e-filing/e-payment portal and official documentation but did not complete verification within this step; CBE website access was blocked by site security for some official PDFs.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: A single light-touch search surfaced a clearly authoritative, operational government tax portal, so the row was moved from the fast (Unknown-confirmation) path to full verification rather than being confirmed as Unknown. The Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) operates an official e-portal (eta.gov.eg / eservice.incometax.gov.eg) that allows registered taxpayers to file income tax and VAT returns online and to pay amounts due directly through the portal via credit/debit card, e-collection intermediaries (Fawry, e-finance) or bank transfer, with an e-receipt issued on completion. This satisfies the top of the scale (4 = Yes). Value Code recalculated from 0 to 4.
revised_comments: Egypt's Tax Authority (ETA) operates an official electronic tax portal (eta.gov.eg / eservice.incometax.gov.eg) through which taxpayers register, file income tax and VAT returns, and settle outstanding tax liabilities online. Payment can be made directly through the portal by credit or debit card, via e-collection intermediaries such as Fawry and e-finance, or by bank transfer to the tax authority's account, with an electronic payment receipt issued on completion. The portal also underpins Egypt's mandatory nationwide e-invoicing and e-receipt system, in force since December 2022.

Definition: Whether digital payment systems and access points (apps, USSD, agents) are designed to accommodate persons with disabilities (visual, hearing, mobility, cognitive impairments), and disability-disaggregated coverage rates if data available.
Comments: 0: Searched for specific accessibility requirements for persons with disabilities in Egypt’s payment systems/apps (e.g., CBE accessibility mandates, WCAG compliance, disability inclusion in financial inclusion strategy) but found no credible, specific evidence within the step.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: A single light-touch search surfaced clear, authoritative regulatory evidence, so the row was moved from the fast (Unknown-confirmation) path to full verification. Since 2021 the Central Bank of Egypt has mandated that banks accommodate persons with disabilities: Braille account-opening and application forms, sign-language-fluent staff (including via video call), screen-reader-compatible digital channels, accessible ATMs (Braille keypads, audio, appropriate lighting) at a minimum of 10% of branches/ATMs, and fee/minimum-balance waivers, under the CBE's Financial Inclusion Strategy (2022-2025). In December 2024 the National Telecom Regulatory Authority extended equivalent requirements to mobile e-wallet services (Braille contracts, sign-language support, screen-reader compatibility, discounted tariffs). This is comprehensive, codified accommodation rather than partial measures, meeting the top of the scale (3 = Yes). Value Code recalculated from 0 to 3.
revised_comments: Egypt's digital payment ecosystem includes explicit, regulator-mandated accessibility provisions for persons with disabilities. Since 2021, Central Bank of Egypt regulation has required banks to adapt at least 10% of branches and ATMs (Braille keypads, audio guidance, appropriate lighting), provide account-opening and application forms in Braille, offer sign-language-fluent customer service including via video call, ensure screen-reader compatibility on digital channels, and waive minimum balances and fees for this group, under the CBE's Financial Inclusion Strategy (2022-2025). In December 2024 the National Telecom Regulatory Authority extended equivalent obligations to mobile e-wallet services, requiring accessible interfaces, sign-language support, Braille contracts and discounted tariffs for persons with disabilities.

Definition: Percentage of government payments (G2P disbursements including salaries, pensions, social transfers) made through instant digital payment system rather than cash or check, reflecting government adoption and modernization.
Comments: 0: Did not find a credible source quantifying the % of all government payments digitized in Egypt (e.g., share of government payroll/procurement/benefits/revenue collected digitally) during the step; only qualitative evidence of e-Finance network and specific programs was found.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: A single light-touch search surfaced substantial evidence of high G2P digitisation, so the row was moved to full verification rather than confirmed as Unknown. The Finance Ministry reported (Jan 2024) that its Government Electronic Payment Gateway processed EGP 8.1 trillion across 607 million transactions from 2019-2023, including EGP 1.07trn in salary payments and 93% activation of the 4.2 million Meeza cards issued to state employees. The National Authority for Social Insurance completed nationwide rollout (Feb 2026) of a fully digital pension disbursement system now covering 10.2 million beneficiaries, and major social transfer programmes (Takaful and Karama, ~20 million individuals) are disbursed via e-Finance-issued prepaid cards. No single official source gives one consolidated percentage across all G2P categories, so the 70-89% estimate is triangulated from several large, high-coverage individual programmes rather than one authoritative aggregate figure; flagged for human review rather than treated as a directly reported statistic. Value Code recalculated from 0 to 4 (70-89%) on this reasoned but indirect basis.
revised_comments: A substantial majority of Egyptian government payments to persons are made digitally rather than in cash. Civil service salaries (paid to around 4.7 million employees) and other beneficiary payments (5.7 million) are processed through the state-owned e-Finance payments network, with 93% of the 4.2 million Meeza payroll cards issued to state employees active. As of February 2026, the National Authority for Social Insurance completed a nationwide digital pension disbursement system covering some 10.2 million beneficiaries, following a phased rollout that began in Cairo in mid-2024. Major cash-transfer programmes such as Takaful and Karama, covering around 20 million individuals, are also disbursed via digital prepaid cards rather than cash.

Definition: Whether refugees, asylum seekers, internally displaced persons, migrants, and stateless persons can legally access and open digital payment accounts, and practical barriers or enablers for these populations.
Comments: 0: Searched for refugee/migrant KYC/payment access programs in Egypt (UNHCR cash assistance delivery channels, refugee mobile wallet access, special KYC rules) but did not secure a credible Egypt-specific source within the step.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: A light-touch search surfaced relevant but mixed evidence, so the row was moved to full verification rather than confirmed as Unknown. UNHCR-registered refugees and asylum seekers in Egypt receive bimonthly cash assistance collected at Egypt Post branches nationwide, authenticated via iris biometric scan or a UNHCR-issued card in place of a national ID; around 16% of the refugee population receives this assistance. This is a dedicated humanitarian cash-collection channel rather than mainstream digital-account access. A CBE circular (August 2024) confirms no blanket restriction on non-resident foreigners opening standard bank accounts, provided a valid residency permit is held, and Egypt's residency rules (from May 2026) tie banking access to a valid residency permit which UNHCR-registered refugees can obtain. However, no source confirms refugee documentation being routinely accepted for mainstream mobile-money accounts, whose Simplified KYC tier is keyed to national ID, which refugees do not hold. This is a genuinely mixed picture (dedicated cash channel plus formal non-discrimination policy, but real barriers to mainstream digital accounts), so it is flagged for human review; Value Code tentatively recalculated from 0 to 2 (Partial) rather than asserted with confidence.
revised_comments: Refugees and asylum seekers in Egypt have partial access to digital payment mechanisms. UNHCR-registered refugees receive bimonthly cash assistance collected at more than 4,000 Egypt Post branches nationwide, authenticated via an iris biometric scan or a UNHCR-issued card rather than a national ID, reaching around 16% of the refugee population. Central Bank of Egypt regulation confirms that non-resident foreign clients are not barred from opening standard bank accounts provided a valid residency permit is held, though mainstream mobile-money accounts under the Central Bank's Simplified KYC regime are keyed to national identification that refugees do not hold, limiting routine access to conventional digital wallets.
